newsitem.title: USA: U.S. West Coast gasoline rises, supply balanced.
newsitem.headline: U.S. West Coast gasoline rises, supply balanced.

text.p: Wholesale prices for U.S. West Coast gasoline rose Thursday, reacting to higher crude futures and tight supplies, despite recent imports, traders said.
NYMEX crude oil for May delivery rose as high as $19.90 a barrel after staying above $18.95, a technical "signal" the contract would rally, according to experts who track trends.

The arrival of four to five cargoes had been factored into the market, traders said, and prices could rise, with West Coast supply falling 2.3 millon barrels short of last year's levels, ahead of heavy demand in the "driving season."
Cargoes included a 486,000 barrel gasoline delivery on the ship Varden, which reached Los Angeles April 3, a trader reported.
Mobil and Chevron refineries have since bought some of its barrels on the spot market, traders said.
Traders could not could give specifics on the four other cargoes.

The balance between supply and demand was reflected in California refinery margins, which rose to $7.50 a barrel in early April, their highest level since the second quarter last year, said Salomon analyst, Paul Ting.
Offers for CARB unleaded gasoline in Los Angeles rose 1.50 to 67 cents, while bids rose a half cent.
Buyers were reluctant to show bids early, anticipating that gasoline's strong premium to the East Coast would attract more supply from Gulf refineries, trader said..

Distillates were flat to softer early, with early heating initially weak. Jet fuel bids fell two cents a gallon in L.A. to 62 cents, while low sulphur diesel in San Francisco remained flat at 61.50/62.50 cents.
